conviction_note: Two-sided. Peers that reported after BNY last spoke point to a modest beat on the reported line and room for an NII guide raise: STT's NII held flat QoQ and STT and JPM both raised NII guides, while BNY's consensus implies NII about 4% down QoQ. Against that, State Street raised its fee and NII guides today, missed revenue by 1% and fell about 6%, the reaction function this season is selling custody prints, and skew is +2.58 to the downside. BNY is already -3.5% today in sympathy and -13.7% since 9/14, which takes some of the downside out. impact_sum +0.5 and impact_scaled +0.16 (p_up 52 x abs 4.0) agree in sign; the scaled number is smaller because the reaction risk keeps p_up near 50.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue ~$5.55B (Zacks $5.56B via search summary; Hudson Labs $5,546M, https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/bny-q3-2026-earnings-revenue-preview-guidance-key-metrics, 2026-09-28), EPS $2.26-2.27 (two sources agree). Zacks-implied NII ~+12.4% YoY on $1,236M = ~$1.39B; fees +8.2% YoY on $3,637M = ~$3.94B. Company guide (Q2 release/call, 2026-07-15): FY26 revenue +10-11% on $20,028M adj (H2 implied $5.46-5.56B/qtr), NII +12-13% on $4,944M (H2 implied $1.36-1.39B/qtr vs Q2 $1,446M), expenses +6-7%. Consensus Q3 revenue sits at the TOP of the guide-implied H2 run rate, so the street already expects a beat/raise.
positioning_check: Short interest ~7.5M shares, 1.1% of float, 1.9 days to cover (StockTitan https://www.stocktitan.net/overview/BNY/, data ~late July 2026; no September figure found) — not crowded, so no squeeze mechanism. Skew +2.58 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.46, ATM spread 43% of mid (implied move 4.03% indicative only). Tape: BNY 157.66 on 2026-09-14 -> 141.03 on 10-13 -> ~136.1 intraday 10-14 (-3.5% today in sympathy with STT -6.1% and NTRS -3.8%; Yahoo chart https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/BNY?range=1mo&interval=1d). BNY underperformed STT/NTRS 9/14-10/13 (-10.5% vs -7.5%/-7.8%). Analyst targets drifting down: Truist 178->172 (9/25), Citi 172->160 (10/5), TD Cowen reinstated Hold $160 (10/8). Insider: CFO sold 31,800 sh at $155.26 on 2026-07-29.

findings.finding: State Street's Q3 (reported 2026-10-14) shows custody revenue holding near Q2: total revenue -1.1% QoQ, servicing fees +1.6% QoQ, NII +0.5% QoQ, average deposits +0.3% QoQ, AUC/A +2.3% QoQ. BNY consensus ($5.55B revenue, fees ~$3.94B, NII ~$1.39B) implies BNY revenue -2.6% QoQ from Q2's $5,698M and NII ~-4% QoQ from $1,446M. Applying STT's QoQ pattern to BNY gives ~$5.63B revenue, about +1.5% vs the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BNY beat Q2 2026 (adj EPS $2.46 vs $2.20, revenue +13%) and rose +5.08%; Q1 2026 beat +2.18%; Oct 2025 -2.03%. 5 of 7 prints up. But STT itself beat EPS today and fell ~6% on a 1% revenue miss.
findings.why_not_priced: BNY consensus was set before STT printed (Hudson preview 9/28) and still embeds a sequential revenue and NII decline; if the market were reading STT's flat NII and deposits across to BNY, BNY would have held up today rather than falling 3.5% in sympathy. The caveat: STT missed its OWN consensus by 1%, so the peer's consensus was not stale. And BNY's CFO said on 9/14 that Q3 was slower than Q2 and deposits slowed. Hence a small size.
findings.independence: Proxy (peer, not BNY's own number). BNY's own Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001390777/000139077726000071/ex991_earningsreleasex2q26.htm) gives the Q2 base that consensus falls from. CFO at Barclays 9/14 said volumes 'kicked back into September' (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/bny-mellon-at-barclays-conference-growth-ai-and-crosssell-push-93CH-4899943).

findings.finding: BNY's FY26 NII guide (+12-13% on FY25 $4,944M = $5,537-5,587M) implies H2 NII of $1,361-1,385M a quarter, 4-6% BELOW Q2's $1,446M. Peers moved the other way after BNY last spoke: State Street raised FY26 NII growth to 15-16% from 14-15% on 10/14 and guided sequential NII growth into Q4; JPMorgan raised 2026 NII guidance on 10/13. The Fed hiked in September and BNY cites ~150bp reinvestment pickup on maturing securities. That leaves room for BNY to raise its NII and total-revenue guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: BNY raised its FY guide (revenue to +10-11% from +6%, NII to +12-13% from +10%) and the stock rose +5.08% on the print day per baseline. STT raised its fee and NII guides on 10/14 and still fell ~6%.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market were pricing a BNY NII raise, BNY would not have sold off in line with STT today, and analyst targets would not have been cut through late Sept/early Oct (Citi 172->160 on 10/5). Counterweight: BNY's CFO said on 9/14 that a +/-100bp rate move has negligible NII effect and that deposit levels drive it, and that deposits slowed in Q3. So a raise depends on the balance sheet, not on rates, and consensus already sits at the top of the revenue guide.
findings.independence: Fed hike in Sept and JPM's NII raise: https://fortune.com/2026/10/13/jpmorgan-goldman-sachs-citigroup-wells-fargo-interest-inflation/ and https://www.mitrade.com/insights/shares-analysis/us-stocks/bank-earnings-day-one-memory-chip-rout-20261014J1406. BNY guide arithmetic from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1390777/000139077726000004/ex991_earningsreleasex4q25.htm and the Q2 release. This finding shares the STT document with finding 1 but rests on a different line (guide, not the quarter).

findings.finding: The custody-bank reaction function this season is negative. State Street raised FY26 fee guidance to 13-14% and NII to 15-16%, beat EPS ($3.69 vs $3.67), and still fell ~6% on 10/14 on a 1% revenue miss, with analysts asking whether the raise was enough. BNY's consensus revenue ($5.55B) already sits at the top of its own guide-implied H2 run rate ($5.46-5.56B), so a merely in-line print plus a modest raise is what the street already holds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: STT -6.1% and NTRS -3.8% on 10/14; BNY -3.5% in sympathy. BNY's own Oct 2025 print was -2.03%. Big banks on 10/13: WFC -3% on a revenue miss despite an EPS beat, JPM -0.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: BNY already fell 3.5% today and the skew is +2.58 to the downside. What remains unpriced is that BNY has to clear a bar above its own guide, and the peer showed a raise is not enough. Short interest is 1.1% of float, so no squeeze offsets a disappointment.
findings.independence: STT/NTRS/BNY price data: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/STT?range=1mo&interval=1d. Revenue-miss-sells pattern: https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nyse/stt/news/earnings/state-street-nysestt-misses-q3-2026-revenue-estimates-stock-drops. Agrees with the skew.

findings.finding: BNY has de-rated into the print: 157.66 on 2026-09-14 (the day of the CFO's Barclays comments) to ~136.1 intraday on 10/14, -13.7%. That is more than STT (-13.1% including today's own print drop) or NTRS (-11.3%). It includes -3.5% today on a peer's print, not on BNY news. The causes are named: the CFO's 'Q3 slower than Q2' and 'deposits slower' remarks, 10y yields near 5.30% and a sector sell-off. The disappointment case is partly in the price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jan 2025 print +8.03% after a pre-print pullback; generally 5 of 7 prints up.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a statement of what IS priced: the run-up is -11.4% (20d) and the stock is 17.5% off its 52-week high. It would be visible in the price if the market expected a beat-and-raise rewarded like July. It is an inference about positioning, not a company number, so it is small.
findings.independence: Analyst target cuts in the same window (Citi, Truist): https://www.thecerbatgem.com/2026/10/13/weekly-investment-analysts-ratings-changes-for-bank-of-new-york-mellon-bny.html. The price series is shared with finding 3 but the reading is opposite in sign. It is resolved as: the peer reaction (finding 3) is the larger risk, and the drawdown partly offsets it.

findings.finding: CFO Dermot McDonogh at Barclays on 2026-09-14 said Q3 was slower than Q2 and deposits slowed 'for sure'. He also said volumes 'kicked back into September' with capital markets strong, and that he 'feels pretty good' about the raised top-line guide with expenses 'well contained'. Both readings come from one document and are netted here as one small positive, because consensus already embeds the slower quarter (-2.6% QoQ revenue).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BNY fell 1.9% the next session (9/15) after these comments (Yahoo chart).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is public and the stock reacted. The residual is that the September volume pickup (STT reported record FX client volumes +31% YoY) may not be fully in a consensus that has BNY fees down ~2.5% QoQ.

findings.finding: The 10-year Treasury yield is near 5.30%, the highest since 2002, after a Fed hike in September with December hike odds at ~88-90%. State Street estimated ~10bp of capital impact per 25bp rise before mitigation. BNY's CET1 was 11.0% at Q2 (down from 11.5% a year earlier) with an 87% YTD payout, so AOCI could constrain the Q3 buyback pace and capital-return commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No BNY-specific history found on a capital-return surprise; the Q2 release paired a 19% dividend raise and $1.1B buyback with the +5.08% day.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission that BNY has not confirmed. STT still guided ~$700M Q4 buybacks, so the peer did not show a capital squeeze. Small.
findings.independence: STT capital sensitivity: https://za.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/earnings-call-transcript-state-street-tops-q3-2026-eps-view-but-shares-fall-93CH-4504885. BNY CET1 11.0%: Q2 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001390777/000139077726000071/ex991_earningsreleasex2q26.htm. Proxy.

findings.finding: BNY is Treasury's financial custodian for Trump Accounts (selected April 2026, launched July 2026). The CFO named Trump Accounts costs as one driver of the expense guide rising to +6-7% from +3-4%. This cost is inside the guide, which implies H2 adjusted expense of $3.43-3.50B a quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July print raised the expense guide and the stock still rose +5.08%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is inside guidance, so close to zero. The only unpriced part would be a Q3 expense step-up above the H2 run rate.

baseline_tension: The skew (+2.58, downside paid), the -11.4% 20-day run-up and today's sympathy drop agree with the negative reaction-function finding. The peer NII and guide-raise evidence cuts against the skew. The net is close to balanced, so p_up sits at 52 rather than leaning on either side.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 and 5 (a verified fact is not a reaction; a peer is a proxy): the STT-QoQ beat finding went from +0.8 to +0.7, because STT beat EPS and still sold off and missed its own consensus.
Lesson 5 (a drawdown is not a cause): the de-rating/positioning finding went from +0.4 to +0.3, kept because the causes are named, not absent.
Lesson 5 (macro-to-company transmission is small): the AOCI/capital-return finding went from -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 7: short interest checked (1.1% float, 1.9 days), not crowded, so the negative reaction-function finding was not shrunk; it agrees with the skew.
Lesson 6: the bar has two agreeing sources and a company guide; no cap applied. The Trump Accounts expense is inside the guide and stays near zero.
Lessons applied once to the scaled side as well: p_up moved from 53 to 52 and abs_move held at 4.0.
